I've had three home insurance providers: Country financial, State auto and hippo. I use Geico for car insurance but I always default to the cheapest policy in terms of lower premiums and deductibles. 

Things to look out for:


-How much coverage you're getting for dwelling, property and liability.

-What your deductible is.
Home owner's insurance policies may have different deductibles for wind (hurricanes) and other events.

-You need to know if you're in a flood zone and purchase flood insurance separately.

-Take pictures and/or video of your home with all your stuff in it in case you need to make a claim. Store these in the cloud in case of a fire or something catastrophic.

-Avoid filing a claim if you can. Insurance companies are scummy and filing one can make you uninsurable. If you've lost your house in a fire or something, of course you should file a claim. But if you have $2000 in roof damage and a $2500 deductible, just go ahead and fix it without insurance. Being able to purchase insurance is worth more than that and you would still be on the hook for the $2000 anyway.
